title: Confluence
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/0/body: When a Fib level lines up with an **old support or resistance**, that area is called **Confluence**. The more reasons that stack up at one price, the more likely price is to react there.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/1/body: First draw Fib on the latest swing, then look to the **left side of the chart**: **old highs and lows**, **round numbers** (like 1.2700 or 60,000) and trendlines. A Fib level that overlaps one of these matters more than the rest.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/1/tip: Confluence is a zone, not an exact price; a few pips of difference is normal.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/2/prompt: Fib is drawn on the swing up and the old resistance is marked. Which Fib level has confluence with it?
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/2/explanat: The 38.2% level (1.08618) sits right in the zone of the old highs (around 1.0860). The broken resistance is now acting as support, and price reacted exactly there.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/3/statemen: Any Fib level on its own is worth as much as a confluence zone.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/3/explanat: A lone level is just one reason. When old support, a round number or a trendline sits at the same price, a reaction becomes more likely.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/4/prompt: GBP/USD swung up from 1.2600 to 1.2800. There's an old support at 1.2700. Which Fib level has confluence with it?
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/4/explanat: The swing is 200 pips and half of it is 100 pips: 1.2800 − 0.0100 = 1.2700. So the 50% level sits on both the old support and a round number.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/5/prompt: EUR/USD swung up from 1.0750 to 1.0950. Look at the left side of the chart too, and put the line on the Fib level that has confluence with an old resistance.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/5/explanat: The swing is 200 pips, so 61.8% = 1.0950 − 0.01236 ≈ 1.0826. Before the swing, price was rejected twice around that same 1.0826; that broken resistance can now act as support. The 50% (1.0850) and 38.2% (about 1.0874) levels have no such confluence.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/6/body: A strong combo: **Fib + old support + round number**. But even the best confluence can break. So wait for a **confirmation candle** and put your stop loss **beyond the whole zone**, not in the middle of it.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/7/prompt: USD/JPY is in an uptrend. Price pulled back to the 50% level, which is also the old resistance and the round number 150.00, and printed a hammer. What do you do?
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/7/explanat: Three reasons stack up at one price: Fib 50% (152 − 2 = 150), the old broken resistance, and a round number. The hammer shows buyers have stepped in. A continuation up is more likely, with a stop below the whole zone.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/8/pairs/0/: Several reasons at one price zone
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l1/steps/8/pairs/3/: Price returning to a broken level
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/0/body: Fib retracements work best **with the trend**: in an uptrend, look for **buys** at the retracement levels, not sells. Before drawing Fib, make sure the trend structure is healthy: **higher highs and higher lows**.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/1/body: Price reaching a level **isn't enough**; wait for a **confirmation candle**. In an uptrend, for example, a **hammer**, **bullish engulfing** or **morning star** at the level shows buyers really stepped in there.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/2/prompt: In an uptrend, price has reached the 61.8% level. What pattern is the last candle?
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/2/explanat: The last candle's green body covers the whole red body before it: a bullish engulfing at 61.8%. That's a confirmation candle in the direction of the uptrend.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/3/prompt: ETH is in a downtrend. Price bounced up to 61.8% of the down swing and printed a bearish engulfing right at that level. What do you do?
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/3/explanat: In a downtrend, retracement levels are where you sell. Price reached 61.8% (2800 + 247.2 = 3047.2), and the bearish engulfing shows sellers are back. A further drop is more likely, with a stop above 78.6%.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/4/body: If price reaches a Fib level and prints a **strong candle against the trend** that closes on the other side of the level, that's a sign **the level is weak**, not an entry. Either wait for the next level or step aside altogether.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/4/tip: Entering on Fib without a confirmation candle is just guessing.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/5/prompt: The trend is up and price has pulled back. Tap the candle that counts as a **buy confirmation candle** inside the golden zone.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/5/explanat: This hammer's long lower wick dipped into the 1.2700 to 1.26764 zone, and it closed above 50%. Buyers pushed price back up from inside the zone.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/6/prompt: In an uptrend, price has reached 61.8%, but the last candle is a big bearish marubozu that closed below the level. What's the best decision?
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/6/options/: Wait; you don't have a buy confirmation yet
Remove your stop so it doesn't get hit
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/6/explanat: A strong bearish candle below the level means sellers are stronger for now. Waiting for a confirmation candle or the next level (like 78.6%) makes more sense.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/7/statemen: A confirmation candle in the trend's direction makes a Fib entry more likely to work, but doesn't guarantee it.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/7/explanat: A confirmation candle shows the other side has stepped into the market, but no pattern is 100%. That's why you always need a stop loss.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/8/prompt: Put the Fib entry checklist in order.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/8/items/1: Draw Fib on the latest swing
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/8/items/2: Wait for price to reach the golden zone
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/8/items/3: Get a confirmation candle with the trend
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/8/items/4: Enter with a stop beyond the zone
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l2/steps/8/explanat: The trend sets the direction, Fib sets the zone, and the confirmation candle sets the timing. The stop loss goes in together with the entry.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/0/body: The most common mistake: drawing Fib on **small, unimportant swings** or in the middle of a **ranging market**. Fib makes sense on a **clear, significant swing**: a low and high that most traders can see too.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/1/title: Mistakes 2 and 3: moving it and expecting precision
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/1/body: The next mistakes are **moving your Fib around** until it fits your opinion, and expecting price to turn **exactly** on the line. Levels are **zones**; a small wick past the line doesn't count as a break.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/1/tip: Write down your drawing rule (say, wick tip to wick tip) and always follow it.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/2/statemen: If price goes a few pips past the 61.8% level and then comes back, the Fib was completely wrong.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/2/explanat: Fib levels are zones, not exact lines. A brief wick past the level and back usually still counts as a reaction to that zone.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/3/prompt: A trader drew Fib on this chart. What's wrong with it?
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/3/options/: The market is ranging; there's no clear swing for Fib
Fib should be drawn on the last candle
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/3/explanat: Price bounces between 1.0800 and 1.0850 without making directional highs and lows. In a range, Fib levels mean nothing special, and price keeps slicing through them.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/4/prompt: A trader started Fib at the swing low but dragged it only to the middle of the swing instead of the swing high. What happens?
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/4/options/: All the levels shift and become invalid
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/4/explanat: Every level is a percentage of the swing's length. If the high point is wrong, the swing length is wrong, and every level lands in the wrong place.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/5/body: Fib **doesn't predict**; it only shows likely zones. Entering without a **stop loss** hoping "61.8% will definitely hold", or ignoring **major economic news**, is the fastest way to lose money with Fib.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/6/prompt: You want to draw Fib on the whole swing up. Tap the swing's **main low**, not the small lows along the way.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/6/explanat: The whole move up started from the lowest low (2296). The later lows are just small pullbacks within the swing; drawing Fib from them changes the swing length and every level.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/7/sentence: A Fib level is a likely ___ for a price reaction, and you shouldn't enter there without a ___.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/7/explanat: Fib only shows where a reaction is likely. Since any level can break, a stop loss is an essential part of every entry.
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/8/prompt: Sara drew Fib on a clear swing up on the 4-hour chart, waited for a bullish engulfing in the golden zone, and put her stop below 78.6%. How's her approach?
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/8/options/: It's solid, but the result still isn't guaranteed
Wrong; Fib only works on the 1-minute chart
Wrong; with Fib you don't need a stop loss
Flawless; this trade will definitely profit
lessons/fibonacci-u3-l3/steps/8/explanat: A clear swing, the golden zone, a confirmation candle and a sensible stop: she avoided all the common mistakes. But no setup is certain, and this trade could still lose.
